queue.claim: Ear long axis leans back about 10-30 degrees from vertical (typical ~20) with the head in Frankfort horizontal, and in Farkas's canon tests it was parallel to the nasal dorsum in only a minority, the ear usually being more upright. This drives the tilt prior N(20, 7).

queue.claim: Vertical position: tragion is at about soft-tissue orbitale level (Frankfort horizontal); top of ear about level with the brow and bottom level with subnasale or up to ~10 mm below; ears are ~5-12 mm longer than nose height (n-sn), so the nasoaural canon mostly fails.

queue.claim: Adult ear length keeps increasing about 0.2 mm per year after maturity (Heathcote, BMJ 1995, 'Why do old men have big ears?'), so ears are several mm to about 1 cm longer at 70 than at 25.
queue.query: Heathcote why do old men have big ears BMJ 1995 ear length increase per year

queue.claim: McDowell otoplasty goals: helix-to-mastoid distance 10-12 mm upper third, 16-18 mm middle, 20-22 mm lower third, with left and right within 3 mm; normal auriculocephalic angle 20-30 degrees (vs <25 degrees with 20 mm or less projection); conchoscaphal angle about 90 degrees.
